question: Should OpenClaw ship opt-in local package dist override replay plus content-inventory fail-closed validation in the core update flow?
rationale: The patch appears technically coherent, but it changes the package update security boundary and future release compatibility behavior, which repository policy leaves to package/security owner intent rather than automation.

options.title: Approve guarded core path
options.body: Accept the default-preserve plus explicit --reapply-local-overrides design and land after package/security owner review confirms the legacy allowlist.

options.title: Ship preservation only
options.body: Keep recovery bundle capture/reporting but remove or defer automatic replay until maintainers want a narrower security model.

options.title: Pause for release audit
options.body: Keep the PR draft until every inventory-less published package and future release cutoff is independently audited.

recommendation.title: Approve guarded core path
recommendation.body: Accept the default-preserve plus explicit --reapply-local-overrides design and land after package/security owner review confirms the legacy allowlist.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned on the PR and has the strongest visible ownership signal across update, packaging, release, and repository policy history.
